subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Cecilia Payne: What Stars Are Made Of
description: One-minute skill: Cecilia Payne: What Stars Are Made Of.

hook.text: Cecilia Payne discovered that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Her thesis was called the most brilliant in astronomy.

buildup.text: In 1925, she applied quantum physics to stellar spectra and found hydrogen dominates—contradicting the accepted view.

discovery.text: Henry Norris Russell discouraged her from publishing the conclusion. Four years later, he reached the same result and took credit.

twist.text: For decades, Payne received little recognition. She became Harvard's first female full professor in astronomy—in 1956.

climax.text: Today she's recognized as having written the most important doctoral thesis in 20th-century astronomy.

punchline.text: She discovered what stars are made of. Credit came decades late.

quiz.question: What did Cecilia Payne discover in her 1925 doctoral thesis?
options: Stars are composed primarily of hydrogen and helium
Stars generate energy through nuclear fission
All stars are the same size but at different distances

details.summary: Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin's 1925 PhD thesis demonstrated that stars are composed primarily of hydrogen and helium — contradicting the prevailing belief that they had the same composition as Earth. Her thesis has been called 'the most brilliant PhD thesis ever written in astronomy.'
details.whyItMatters: Payne's discovery revealed the true nature of stars and the universe's dominant composition. Despite being initially forced to retract her conclusion by a senior astronomer, she was eventually proven completely correct.
takeaways: Payne proved stars are mostly hydrogen and helium in 1925
This contradicted the prevailing view of Earth-like composition
Her PhD thesis is considered the most brilliant in astronomy

faq.question: Why was Payne's conclusion initially rejected?
faq.answer: Henry Norris Russell, the era's most influential astronomer, convinced her to add a note saying her result was 'almost certainly not real.' Four years later, Russell reached the same conclusion using different methods and published it — receiving much of the credit.

faq.question: How did Payne determine stellar composition?
faq.answer: She applied the new theory of ionization physics (by Meghnad Saha) to stellar spectra. By analyzing how spectral line strengths change with temperature and relating this to element abundances, she showed that the enormous hydrogen and helium abundances explained observed spectra perfectly.
